01 / The idea

There may be a book inside your story.

You bring the experiences, convictions, knowledge, lessons and voice. The work begins by uncovering what is already there and giving it structure.

01 — UNCOVER

Find the story.

We identify the experiences, turning points, lessons, people, challenges and moments that give your story meaning.

02 — SHAPE

Find the message.

We clarify what the story is really about, what changed and what the reader should understand or take away.

03 — STRUCTURE

Build the direction.

We organize the material into a logical narrative and chapter direction that can support the next stage.

02 / One-month development

Four weeks. One clear objective.

The planned one-month window is for story development and preparation — not a promise that the final book will be completed in one month.

WEEK 01 — DISCOVER

Story Discovery

Gather the raw material: experiences, memories, turning points, lessons, conflicts and breakthroughs.

WEEK 02 — CLARIFY

Message & Meaning

Identify the central idea, transformation, reader and message. Flag what needs clarification.

WEEK 03 — STRUCTURE

Story Architecture

Arrange the material, reduce repetition, identify gaps and establish chapter direction.

WEEK 04 — PREPARE

Book-Ready Document

Review, organize and prepare the agreed story-development document for hand-off.

Timeline condition: the one-month schedule assumes timely participation, including supplying information, answering questions and reviewing agreed stages. Delays can extend the working timeline.
03 / The deliverable

What you actually receive.

STORY OVERVIEW

What happened.

A clear understanding of the experience and why the story matters.

CENTRAL MESSAGE

What it means.

The core lesson, testimony, transformation or idea holding the story together.

TIMELINE

What came next.

Key events and turning points arranged in a useful sequence where appropriate.

CHAPTER DIRECTION

How it flows.

A proposed structure showing how the story can be organized into chapters.

KEY MATERIAL

What matters.

Important experiences, scenes, lessons, reflections and supporting information gathered during development.

HAND-OFF

What happens next.

A structured foundation that can be taken to the professional the client chooses for final manuscript development.

04 / Critical clarification

This is not the finished book.

The service described here develops and prepares your story. At the end, you receive the agreed Book-Ready Story Document.

You choose who takes it from there. You may select a writer, ghostwriter, editor, publisher or another qualified professional to convert the prepared material into the final manuscript/book.

That next-stage professional is selected independently by you. Their price, agreement, timeline, writing scope, publishing arrangements and other services are separate from this engagement.
